title: Subclinical thyroid disease: scientific review and guidelines for diagnosis and management
authors: Surks MI, Ortiz E, Daniels GH, Sawin CT, Col NF, Cobin RH, et al.
funder: not stated in the publisher page text. Representatives of the American Thyroid Association and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists formed the planning committee, with the Endocrine Society; continuing medical education credit was provided through the Endocrine Society; nonendocrinologist panelists received an honorarium.
authorConflicts: Potential conflicts of interest were obtained from panelists and speakers and printed in the conference materials, not in the article.
result: The panel did not recommend routine levothyroxine for TSH between 4.5 and 10 mIU/l, finding insufficient evidence of therapeutic benefit and a small likelihood of symptom improvement. It judged levothyroxine reasonable for TSH above 10 mIU/l, while stating that evidence that treatment lowers cholesterol and improves symptoms is inconclusive.
